papers.abstract: We investigate electron-positron pair production in spatially homogeneous, time-dependent polarized electric fields using the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism, focusing on the effects of symmetric and asymmetric quadratic frequency chirping and the carrier-envelope phase (CEP). Our analysis reveals how these field parameters govern both the momentum-space structure and the overall yield of the produced pairs. Frequency chirping substantially reshapes the momentum distributions by modifying their interference patterns and peak occupations. The momentum distributions are particularly sensitive to weak chirping, whereas strong chirping produces pronounced oscillatory and ring-like structures across all polarization states. The total pair yield increases with chirp strength, with symmetric chirping consistently producing a higher yield than asymmetric chirping for the parameter range considered. Moreover, the sensitivity of the total number density to polarization decreases progressively with increasing chirp strength, becoming negligible in the strongly chirped regime. The CEP further modifies the momentum distributions by altering their shapes and relative peak occupations, with the extent of these changes depending on the polarization state. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring external-field configurations that optimize the yield of Schwinger pair production.

papers.title: Brownian GPDs: A Stochastic Calculus Approach to Generalized Parton Distributions from Integral Constraints
papers.abstract: We present a stochastic calculus approach for modeling generalized parton distribution functions using information provided from lattice QCD calculations of Mellin moments, without assuming a functional form. Reconstructing the underlying dependence on the partonic momentum fraction from a limited number of moments constitutes an intrinsically non-unique inverse problem. Our goal is to provide a model agnostic way to determine GPDs subject to integral constraints. Thus, we derive and show usage of a controlled Langevin approach based on stochastic calculus and Brownian motion. The method combines a variational formulation, based on minimizing a Dirichlet action subject to the imposed constraints, with stochastic dynamics that generates an ensemble of admissible functions. The resulting ensemble provides a preferred reconstruction and characterizes the variability associated with incomplete integral information within the chosen stochastic model. The framework can accommodate general integral kernels and prescribed function values, offering a flexible approach to reconstructing functions from indirect constraints. Beyond its application to GPD phenomenology, the method provides a general strategy for investigating inverse problems in which integral observables are known but the underlying functional dependence remains undetermined. The approach may have more general applications beyond the scope of studying 3D hadron structure, and it is particularly useful in situations where we know definite integrals of functions with kernels, but do not know the underlying function.

papers.title: Strangeness suppression, the $φ$ meson and $Λ\barΛ$ spin correlations from exact strangeness conservation at the quark level
papers.abstract: In small collision systems strange hadrons are suppressed, and the suppression grows with the number of strange quarks. Exact strangeness conservation in a finite volume accounts for this, but when it is imposed on hadrons it leaves the $φ$ meson unsuppressed, contrary to observation. We impose the conservation law on the strange quarks in a causally connected cluster, before hadronization, and count separately the combinations of a strange quark with the antiquark created together with it. A pair created from the vacuum cannot form a $φ$, a pair created from a gluon can only if it loses its color. With one function of multiplicity, the mean number of strange quarks per cluster, the model describes kaons, $φ$, $Ξ$ and $Ω$ in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC; the data require that about half of the same-pair combinations are excluded from the $φ$, and reject both an unsuppressed $φ$ and a $φ$ built only from different pairs at about five standard deviations. The same-pair combinations are those that carry the spin correlation observed in $Λ\barΛ$ production, whose dilution is thereby tied to the $φ$ suppression and is predicted to decrease with multiplicity

papers.title: Evolution of multihadron fragmentation functions with nonperturbative behavior
papers.abstract: QCD calculations that use multihadron fragmentation functions usually involve multiple invariant mass scales simultaneously, with only one being the hard scale associated with an overall hard process. The other scales are associated with relative internal motion intrinsic to the fragmenting parton and the multihadron system. Nonperturbative contributions to this later type of dependence attract interest for their association with intrinsic partonic structures, but care is needed in disentangling the truly nonperturbative effects from perturbative behavior and relating the former to universal nonperturbative matrix elements. To this end, we show how to evolve collinear multihadron fragmentation functions in a way that accounts for the simultaneous presence of these extra scales. The general multihadron fragmentation functions evolve in the same way as ordinary single hadron fragmentation functions, with the dependence on the extra scales separated out. We use this to unify treatments of perturbative and nonperturbative effects in multihadron systems in a way that optimizes for interpretations focused on partonic structure.

papers.title: Displaced tracks as a signal of dark matter co-annihilation: a case study using inert doublet model at $e^+e^-$ collider
papers.abstract: Dark sector containing heavy (charged) particles with small mass splitting with dark matter (DM) can co-annihilate and produce correct relic density, evading direct detection bounds. In such compressed spectra, the charged state can be long-lived and decay to DM along with a very soft charged particle, giving rise to distinctive disappearing or kink track signatures at colliders. As an example, we consider the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), where the charged scalar $H^\pm$ can be nearly degenerate with the neutral DM state ($H^0$), and produce a soft pion ($π^\pm$) when it decays. We investigate this signature at a future $e^+e^-$ collider, focusing on electroweak $H^+H^-$ pair production and its displaced decays. By varying the mass splitting, we explore the transition from prompt soft-particle signatures to long-lived and disappearing-track signatures. Our analysis demonstrates the potential of future lepton colliders to probe the interplay between the charged-particle lifetime, its decay probability within the tracking volume, and the production rate sensitivity to the compressed DM scenarios over a broad range of masses, allowed by cosmological constraints.

papers.title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
papers.abstract: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$σ$-meson interpolating operators. The analysis is performed using three gauge ensembles, including one ensemble simulated with two degenerate light, a strange, and a charm quark with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical value. We solve the generalized eigenvalue problem that arises from the matrix of correlators and show that the three-point function for the light sigma-term obtained using the optimal linear combination of interpolating operators has substantially reduced time dependence without loss of statistical precision. We apply Laplace filtering and investigate residual excited-state contributions in the extraction of $σ_{πN}$. Using the same optimal linear combination of correlators as for $σ_{πN}$ for the strange sigma-term we also observe suppressed excited state contributions over an extended range of source--sink time separations. For the charm sigma-term, we observe negligible time dependence within the large statistical uncertainties, and these improvements show no significant effect.

papers.title: Thermal properties of the $ρ$ meson from a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model
papers.abstract: The thermal properties of the \(ρ\) meson are revisited within the soft-wall AdS/QCD framework. The dilaton background is calibrated against lattice QCD screening-mass data through a neural-network-assisted inverse procedure. Using this calibrated background, we compute the temporal vector spectral function and the lowest vector quasi-normal modes. The pole mass \(m_{\mathrm{pole}}(T)\) and thermal width \(Γ(T)\) are then extracted from the corresponding complex quasi-normal mode frequencies. Adopting the vanishing real part of the quasi-normal mode frequency, \(ω_{\mathrm{Re}}(T_d)=0\), as a criterion for meson dissociation, we estimate \(T_d\approx168\,\mathrm{MeV}\). As the temperature increases, the thermal width grows, and the spectral function evolves from a narrow Breit-Wigner-like resonance peak into a transport peak, confirming the QNM prediction that the vanishing of the pole mass is accompanied by the emergence of a transport peak and making it difficult to identify a quasiparticle peak. A numerical extraction of the dispersion relation shows that the propagator can be described by a finite-temperature simple-pole form with momentum-dependent thermal width, characterized by a diffusion coefficient \(D(T)\) and an effective propagation speed \(u(T)\), whose temperature dependences are also extracted. This form modifies the usual relation between the screening and pole masses. These results may provide a useful reference for effective studies of the hot hadronic medium.

papers.title: Transport of hard probes in the glasma
papers.abstract: The quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC thermalizes from an out-of-equilibrium state of strong classical gluon fields known as the glasma. Jets and heavy quarks, produced in the initial scatterings, traverse these pre-equilibrium fields, but the glasma stage is neglected in phenomenology, which may bias the extracted QGP transport coefficients. This thesis studies its impact on jet and heavy quark transport. The glasma is described in the Color Glass Condensate framework by solving the classical Yang-Mills equations on a real-time lattice. The fields initially form longitudinal electric and magnetic flux tubes whose transverse correlation length is set by the saturation scale $Q_s$. Probes are studied with both classical transport equations and quantum evolution in the light-front Hamiltonian approach. The transport coefficients for jets and heavy quarks are much larger than in the QGP and anisotropic between transverse and longitudinal directions. The azimuthal decorrelation of back-to-back $c\bar{c}$ pairs in the glasma is comparable to that from the QGP, making $D\bar{D}$ angular correlations a potentially measurable glasma signature. The glasma also modifies the nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, though the effect is moderate compared to the nuclear parton distribution contribution. A systematic gauge-invariance analysis shows that the distinction between kinetic and canonical momenta is essential when comparing classical and quantum results, and that Coulomb gauge fixing largely reduces gauge artifacts. Finally, the eikonal quantum evolution of a high-energy quark is studied with time-dependent Basis Light-Front Quantization. The resulting momentum broadening agrees with the classical estimates and lays the groundwork for including quantum radiation.

papers.title: Spin and 3D structure: theoretical advances
papers.abstract: Theoretical studies of hadron structure have made important progress since the previous DIS workshop in 2025. This talk reviews selected new results and developments, with a focus on spin dependent parton distributions, on transverse-momentum distributions and their rapidity dependence, on generalised parton distributions, and on the evaluation of power corrections.

papers.title: Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics
papers.abstract: We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.

papers.title: The dead-cone effect in charm, bottom and top quark jets in angular and momentum space
papers.abstract: The dead-cone effect reflects the mass dependence of QCD radiation from heavy quarks. We investigate this phenomenon from charm and bottom to top quarks using two-dimensional angular distributions and single-particle inclusive momentum spectra. The angular distributions illustrate the depletion of radiation around the heavy-quark direction, while the momentum spectra provide a quantitative observable of the effect. For charm and bottom jets, fragmentation functions reconstructed from LEP data at the $Z$ pole exhibit a strong suppression of high-momentum particles, quantitatively described within the Modified Leading Logarithmic Approximation of perturbative QCD. The analysis is extended to $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV using Monte Carlo simulations. A hypothetical stable-top sample isolates the primary top-quark radiation pattern, whereas the physical decay $t\to bW$ introduces coherent radiation from the $tb$ colour dipole, obscuring the primary dead cone. By exploiting the dependence on the $b$-quark emission angle $Θ_b$, we reconstruct the primary top-quark parton momentum spectrum through extrapolation to $Θ_b\to0$. In contrast, the small-angle gluon and parton distributions do not converge to the stable-top dead-cone pattern because of radiation from the decay $b$ quark. These findings establish the inclusive momentum spectrum as a robust quantitative observable of the top-quark dead-cone effect and provide a unified description of mass-dependent QCD radiation from charm to top.

papers.title: The stability of non-Abelian $A_4$ vortices in $SO(3)$ gauge theory
papers.abstract: We study the linear energetic stability of non-Abelian vortices in an $SO(3)$ gauge-Higgs theory with residual gauge group $A_4$. In our previous work, we identified two families of such vortices associated with order-two and order-three elements of $A_4$, and found Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior at special ratios of the Higgs and gauge-boson mass scales. Here, we investigate their stability against $SO(3)$ gauge and Higgs perturbations by analyzing the second order variation of the vortex tension using analytical and numerical methods. In particular, when all relevant mass scales are equal, we prove linear stability for all vortices in the order-three family. By contrast, at the same mass point, we prove that a vortex in the order-two family is unstable. Thus, although both vortex families exhibit Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior in their reduced equations at this mass point, their stability properties in the full $SO(3)$ theory are qualitatively different.

papers.title: MoEDAL-MAPP: the first dedicated search experiment at the LHC
papers.abstract: This special issue brings together a collection of original research articles and review papers addressing topics directly related to the MoEDAL-MAPP experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The experiment is designed to search for (meta-)stable, anomalously ionising particles predicted by theoretical extensions of the Standard Model. Several contributions explore the theoretical and phenomenological aspects of models of particular relevance to the experiment, including scenarios involving magnetic monopoles, highly electrically charged particles, and millicharged particles. Other contributions focus on experimental developments, highlighting novel detection techniques and technological advances aimed at identifying these unconventional signatures and probing new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

papers.title: The Semileptonic B Frontier: LHC, B-factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision
papers.abstract: This review document summarizes the main outcomes and key theoretical and experimental developments discussed at the workshop ``The Semileptonic $B$ Frontier: LHC, $B$-Factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision'', held at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati on 16--18 February, https://agenda.infn.it/event/49469/. Bringing together experimentalists and theorists, the meeting addressed recent advances and outstanding challenges in both charged-current ($b \to c/u\,\ellν$) and neutral-current ($b \to s\,\ell^+\ell^-$) semileptonic $b$-hadron decays. We synthesize current experimental measurements from Belle, Belle~II, and LHCb with state-of-the-art theoretical inputs---including Lattice QCD determinations, Heavy Quark Expansion (HQE) frameworks, and QED radiative corrections. In addition to reviewing the status of CKM matrix elements, hadronic form factor extractions, and Lepton Flavor Universality (LFU) tests, this report highlights novel observables and fitting techniques designed to maximize the sensitivity of future analyses and guide upcoming data-taking campaigns.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
papers.abstract: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% confidence-level bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $ε$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \ll ω_c$.

papers.title: Decoherence as a Detector-Resolution Flow
papers.abstract: We consider the QED final-state radiation modeled by $γγ^\ast\toπ^+π^-+X$, including its finite-temperature generalization, as an open quantum system, and study the evolution of the pion-pair momentum density matrix as the detector resolution scale is varied. We derive an explicit relation between the Lindblad jump operator and the Wilson line associated with soft photon radiation. We find that real emission and virtual correction serve as two separate contributions to momentum decoherence, and together they give rise to the real--virtual cancellation at the density-matrix level. The external finite-temperature photon bath modifies the decoherence rate by a Bose factor consistent with the Feynman--Vernon influence-functional approach. We emphasize that our conclusions also apply to hard fermion production thanks to the universality of the soft radiation.

papers.title: Superhorizon enhancement of the hydrodynamic GW tail in Standard Model embedded warm inflation
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. To address this situation, we define a model-independent transfer function for GWs generated by hydrodynamic (or other white-noise) fluctuations at any time. Employing appropriate variables, we show how this transfer function, together with the simpler vacuum one, can be determined numerically for a general expansion history. The results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation scenarios, including both the vacuum and hydrodynamic parts. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).

papers.title: Thermal spectral functions of heavy and exotic Mesons from a hQCD at finite density
papers.abstract: In this work, we study spectral functions of heavy and exotic mesons in a self-consistent Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton model at finite temperature and chemical potential, where the dilaton is allowed to back-react on the geometry. A non-quadratic dilaton profile is introduced to reproduce the nonlinear Regge trajectories of heavy-flavor mesons, and the corresponding spectral functions are computed for charmonium, bottomonium, tetraquark, and hybrid channels. In all cases, increasing either temperature or chemical potential suppresses and broadens the quasiparticle peaks, signaling sequential in-medium dissociation; for each radial family, the 2S-like state melts before the 1S-like state. The predicted melting temperatures obey the mass ordering $T_{\rm melt}^{π_1(1400)}<T_{\rm melt}^{J/ψ}<T_{\rm melt}^{Z_c(3900)}<T_{\rm melt}^{Υ(1S)}$, with $T_{\rm melt}\simeq 1.08,\ 2.96,\ 4.44$, and $5.93\,T_c$, respectively, so heavier states remain bound up to higher temperatures. These results provide quantitative, testable predictions for heavy-ion experiments probing tetraquark and hybrid mesons in hot and dense QCD matter.

papers.title: Binding energies in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ fermion--antifermion channels from the ladder Bethe-Salpeter and Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we calculate the binding energies of an equal-mass fermion--antifermion system in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ channels from the ladder Bethe--Salpeter (BS) equation with scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector exchange. The results are compared with those of the Schrödinger equation with the corresponding leading static interaction in two regimes: pointlike massless exchange at weak coupling and finite-mass exchange with monopole form factors at stronger coupling. For the BS calculation, we use two independent numerical methods based on momentum-space integral equations and coordinate-space differential equations. The differential-equation method gives estimated relative binding-energy errors below $10^{-9}$ in both regimes. For massless vector exchange in Coulomb gauge, the numerical results are consistent with the uncrossed-ladder perturbative spectrum through the $O(mα^5)$ terms. The results for massless scalar exchange and vector exchange in Feynman gauge are consistent with the common Wick--Cutkosky expansion through order $mα^3$. For finite exchange masses, the differences from the leading static Schrödinger spectra at the same masses, couplings, and form factors depend strongly on the exchange and channel. Scalar exchange gives nearly degenerate channels with much weaker binding than the Schrödinger reference. In contrast, vector exchange with only the metric term retained gives stronger binding than the Schrödinger reference in $0^{-+}$ and weaker binding in $1^{--}$. Notably, retaining the full Proca numerator substantially increases the vector binding in both channels. Pseudoscalar exchange also supports bound states and favors $1^{--}$, although its leading static central interaction vanishes.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

papers.title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small $x$ from leading-neutron electroproduction data
papers.abstract: We revisit the extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the pion in a global QCD analysis of pion--nucleus Drell--Yan and leading-neutron (LN) electroproduction data, in view of recent suggestions that uncertainties on the pion PDFs at small parton momentum fraction $x$ are dramatically underestimated. We perform a set of controlled fits that vary the LN data coverage, PDF parametrization, and positivity constraints, determining both the PDFs and pion-nucleon splitting functions simultaneously. While the use of a restricted H1 LN data sample used by the Fantômas group is found to enlarge the PDF uncertainties and admit solutions with vanishing gluon PDFs, our global analysis provides a good description of an extended H1 and ZEUS LN database, significantly reducing the parametrization dependence and strongly disfavoring a zero gluon distribution.

papers.title: Bottom-Charm $[bc]$ Diquark Masses from QCD Laplace Sum-Rules
papers.abstract: Constituent mass predictions for bottom-charm $[bc]$ color-antitriplet diquarks are generated using QCD Laplace sum rules. We calculate the diquark correlator within the operator product expansion to next-to-leading-order (NLO), including terms proportional to the four- and six-dimensional gluon and six-dimensional quark condensates. Existing analytic expressions for the resulting multi-scale master integrals are insufficient for these calculations, so we utilize numerical $D$-dimensional loop integration techniques. The sum rule analyses stabilize in all four channels yielding constituent masses in GeV of: scalar ($0^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$, pseudoscalar ($0^-$) $(6.04\pm0.60)$, axial vector ($1^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$ and vector ($1^-$) $(5.99\pm0.60)$. These constituent mass results are discussed in comparison with values used in diquark models of tetraquark hadronic states. We also summarize QCD sum rule predictions for diquark masses for all possible quark-flavor combinations, providing QCD-based criteria for assessing the diquark mass parameters used in constituent diquark models of hadrons.

papers.title: Chandra-JWST Probing the Effects of Moderate X-Ray Superflares on Protoplanetary Disks
papers.abstract: Powerful X-ray flares from young stars may rapidly alter the physical and chemical conditions of their planet-forming disks, but direct observational tests remain scarce. We present a Chandra-JWST/NIRSpec study of infrared spectral variability associated with pre-main-sequence (PMS) X-ray flares in the Orion Nebula. Combining six Chandra/ACIS-I observations with three NIRSpec-MOS visits, we analyze two-epoch spectra of 10 X-ray Flare stars and 12 matched non-flaring Controls among 84 observed disk-bearing PMS stars. We investigate three diagnostics: narrow 2.8-4.3 micron features, HI Br-alpha, and the CO fundamental band. Flare stars show tentative evidence for relatively fewer variable narrow features at longer wavelengths than Controls, while feature incidence decreases strongly with projected distance from the dominant ionizing O star Theta1 Ori C. Most classifiable features appear in absorption. These properties suggest that at least some features may arise in externally irradiated disk atmospheres and/or associated photoevaporative flows, with their apparent epoch-to-epoch variability potentially reflecting spatial sampling of such locally structured material rather than intrinsic temporal changes. Br-alpha behaves differently: flare stars show systematically stronger variability and uniquely exhibit absorption-core profiles, suggesting control by magnetospheric accretion and stellar magnetic processes rather than disk irradiation. The CO fundamental band shows no significant flare-associated variability, consistent with thermochemical models predicting weak responses to moderate X-ray superflares. This pilot study demonstrates the potential of coordinated Chandra-JWST observations to probe how young stellar magnetic activity affects planet-forming environments, motivating future monitoring to build larger superflare samples and extend them into the rare X-ray mega-flare regime.

papers.title: Infrared-Finite Positivity Bounds in 4D Gravity
papers.abstract: We formulate an S-matrix bootstrap in an exactly flat half-space, where boundary reflection provides geometric infrared control for four-dimensional gravity. Under the channel positivity conditions, we obtain an infrared-finite positivity bound on local four-scalar Wilson coefficients that includes a finite gravitational correction of order $G_N$ and is derived from the full UV absorptive spectrum without specifying a UV theory, imposing a spectral ansatz, requiring weak coupling or expanding the spectrum perturbatively. At fixed dimensionless external state parameters, the coefficient of the leading gravitational correction is independent of the EFT scale and requires neither an arbitrary soft resolution scale nor a model-dependent UV scale. Gaussian wave-packet scattering localizes interactions within the flat region and directly probes bulk Wilson coefficients while exponentially suppressing sensitivity to the boundary. Long-range gravitons remain sensitive to the boundary and give a finite contribution. The smearing functional passes numerical positivity tests with general half-space absorptive kernels in both crossed channels. An explicit string example shows how boundary reflection suppresses the collective contribution of string resonances to the absorptive part of the amplitude, connecting infrared control of low-energy scattering to the UV spectrum of quantum gravity in the same dispersion relation. The framework opens a route to infrared-finite constraints on effective interactions across particle physics and gravity.

papers.title: Effective Fermion-Photon Vertex in a Rotating Relativistic Medium: Tree-Level Structure
papers.abstract: We study the tree-level fermion-photon effective vertex for on-shell particles in a relativistic environment undergoing rigid rotation at zero temperature. The rotational background breaks translational invariance in the transverse plane and introduces a preferred direction, leading to a distinct decomposition of the vertex into longitudinal and transverse structures with respect to the rotation axis. Using fermion and photon modes constructed in the rotating frame, we derive the corresponding selection rules and show that the energy and the longitudinal component of the momentum are conserved, whereas no independent transverse momentum-conservation condition arises. Instead, the transverse dependence is governed by radial integrals involving three Bessel functions, whose support constrains the magnitudes of the transverse momentum projections. The vertex can be organized in a circular basis for the transverse components and a Cartesian basis along the rotation axis, and expressed in terms of six Dirac structures. Their coefficients define 24 form-factor components associated with the photon-mode components, physical photon states, and spin-dependent structures induced by the rotating background. We also verify current conservation and gauge invariance of the resulting tree-level matrix element under the boundary conditions considered. These results provide the tree-level structure of the fermion-photon interaction in rotating relativistic matter and establish the basis for the study of radiative corrections in vortical backgrounds.

papers.title: Pythia-Contrib: a modular contribution framework for the Pythia 8 event generator
papers.abstract: Pythia is a general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator used in particle, astroparticle, and nuclear physics, by theorists and experimentalists, to simulate particle collisions. Because of the size and diversity of the user community, it is challenging to address all of the needs for new and varied physics models. This paper describes the Pythia-Contrib system, which allows for third-party developers to contribute code to Pythia without introducing external software dependencies to the Pythia code base.

papers.title: Quasiparticle Modeling of Strongly Magnetized Strange Quark Systems
papers.abstract: We examine spin-polarized Strange Quark Matter and the complex structure of Strange Quark Stars in the existence of a strong magnetic field. Our framework uses a quasiparticle model, en hanced by a QCD-informed effective quark mass dependent on both chemical potential value and magnetic field strength. The resulting Equation of State yields an energy per baryon below the iron limit, supporting the hypothesis that the actual ground state of matter is strange matter. The Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff expressions are solved and find that the maximum stellar mass decreases with the degree of spin polarization, reaching as high as 2.35 Mo with a related radius 12.33 km. Furthermore, the model predictions for mass, radius, and surface redshift are in excel lent conformance to observational limitations for the massive pulsar PSR J0952-0607. These results highlight the crucial role of quasiparticle medium effects and strong magnetic fields in describing dense matter.

papers.title: Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory and its application to $X_b$
papers.abstract: Following the discovery of the exotic state $X(3872)$ in the charmonium spectrum, the possible existence of an analogous state, $X_b$, in the bottomonium sector has attracted considerable attention of the hadronic physics community. In this work, we lay the ground for the development of Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$χ$EFT), that allows us to include both quark and hadron degrees of freedom as well as the full complexity of the meson-exchange potential in a systematic way. For illustration, the formalism to leading order (LO) is applied to the system of $χ_{b1}$ states and in particular the $X_b$. The two parameters that are present at this order are constrained using experimental information on the bottomonium spectrum together with lattice input on static quark-antiquark potentials, including string breaking effects. The framework identifies the observed $1^{++}$ state at 10.513 GeV with a predominantly molecular $X_b$, the bottom counterpart of the $X(3872)$, and predicts an additional predominantly compact bottomonium state at 10.544 GeV, about 60 MeV below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.

papers.title: Two-loop $gg\to AA$ amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity
papers.abstract: The two-loop amplitudes for pseudoscalar pair production in gluon fusion, $gg\to AA$, with each pseudoscalar emitted from its own effective gluon vertex, are known in closed form, but large cancellations near threshold obscure their analytic structure. We expand the IR-finite amplitudes in the pseudoscalar velocity $β_A$ through $β_A^6$ at fixed scattering angle. All inverse powers of $β_A$ and the odd powers through $β_A^5$ cancel, and at leading power the angular dependence enters only through $\ln(2p_T/m_A)$. We identify this logarithm with the double parton scattering (DPS) singularity: with the overall constant fixed at threshold, the factorisation formula of Gaunt and Stirling reproduces the velocity dependence of its one-loop coefficient in the forward limit to $3\times10^{-15}$, and a one-loop $gg\to HH$ analysis confirms the corresponding CP-even weight. At two loops the equal-helicity amplitude grows as $\ln^3p_T$, with the leading logarithmic ratio of planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, while the opposite helicity amplitude, which has no one-loop DPS logarithm, grows as $\ln^2p_T$. In the finite virtual correction, relative to the squared tree amplitude, the highest logarithm at order $α_s^2$ is $-\tfrac{7}{64}α_s^2N_c^2\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. For $β_A\leq0.2$ the series reproduce the unexpanded amplitudes with relative errors of at most $6.77\times10^{-5}$ at the tested points; they provide this two-loop contribution to the hard function for soft-gluon resummation of the pair invariant-mass distribution near $m_{AA}=2m_A$ and are released with code for their numerical evaluation.

papers.title: Audible curvaton: modulated phase transition as the origin of large-scale curvature perturbations and gravitational wave anisotropies
papers.abstract: We propose a post-inflationary first-order phase transition modulated by a light spectator field as the origin of primordial large-scale curvature perturbations. Spectator fluctuations acquired during inflation modulate the bubble nucleation history, generating curvature perturbations together with correlated intrinsic gravitational-wave (GW) anisotropies. We show that this mechanism can reproduce the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while producing a loud stochastic GW background in the frequency bands of space-based detectors such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. A concrete benchmark yields strongly enhanced intrinsic GW anisotropies and a local primordial non-Gaussianity signal within reach of future large-scale-structure surveys.

papers.title: A spurionic interpretation of RG-stable parameter relations in the two-Higgs-doublet model
papers.abstract: Recent work on the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) has uncovered basis-invariant relations among the parameters in the scalar potential that are stable under renormalization group (RG) evolution but do not coincide with any of the standard Higgs-family or Generalized-$\mathrm{CP}$ symmetry classes of the scalar sector. These relations have subsequently been reformulated in terms of so-called GOOFy transformations. In this paper, we show that the same fixed surface admits a conventional interpretation in terms of spurions. The gauge-covariant kinetic terms of the 2HDM possess a Higgs-family $\mathrm{U}(2)_H$ symmetry, and the couplings in the potential may be organized into irreducible spurions under its nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)_H$ subgroup. We first explain the one-loop closure in the spurion language and then establish stability to all orders in the scalar and gauge couplings in any mass-independent scheme. General Yukawa couplings introduce additional Higgs-family covariants and can spoil the scalar-sector selection rule. We therefore consider the six conventional Higgs-family and Generalized-$\mathrm{CP}$ symmetries of the 2HDM, imposed as exact symmetries of the full Lagrangian, and show that closure is controlled by whether the relevant Higgs-family triplet contains an invariant direction. The spurion formulation thus provides a basis-covariant and conventional group-theoretic explanation of the RG stability of the 2HDM parameter relations.

papers.title: Exothermic dark-photon dark matter and the LZ high-recoil event: finite-reheating constraints
papers.abstract: An excited dark-matter state can produce a high-energy nuclear recoil by releasing its mass splitting in a collision. Motivated by the $248$~keV LUX--ZEPLIN candidate, we study freeze-in of a $45$~GeV pseudo-Dirac particle with a $1$~MeV splitting and a $1$~GeV dark photon during non-instantaneous reheating. We choose a recoil normalization compatible with the published INTEGRAL/SPI three-photon decay limit. It predicts $0.43$ events in the LZ window and retains the reference recoil shape. Including both dark-photon and $Z$ exchange, we calculate production and entropy dilution for backgrounds with $T\propto a^{-α}$ and $ρ_φ\propto a^{-3(1+ω)}$. For $\Tmax=m_χ$, the observed abundance requires $\Trh=1.32$~GeV for matter-like constant-width reheating, $3.09$~GeV for quartic oscillations with scalar decay, and $0.588$~GeV for quartic oscillations with constant width, compared with $4.10$~GeV for instantaneous reheating. These finite-reheating solutions are insensitive to increasing $\Tmax$ above $m_χ$. For $\Tmax\geq m_χ$, adiabatic kination has no solution with $\Trh>5.96$~MeV, the BBN-motivated cutoff adopted for our scans. At $α_D=10^{-10}$, the estimated thermal-mediator source is below $0.2\%$ of the Standard Model source, and self-conversion does not appreciably deplete the excited population. The calculation relates an exothermic recoil benchmark to the production and dilution history before radiation domination.

papers.title: Direct Detection of Solar Neutrinos to Probe Tensions and Break Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiments
papers.abstract: Long-baseline (LBL) accelerator experiments are sensitive not only to the standard neutrino oscillation parameters but also to new physics. Currently, there exists a tension between NOvA and T2K data that can be explained by vector non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) with complex couplings, which in turn introduce degeneracies in LBL measurements. We demonstrate that dark matter direct detection experiments can use their measurements of solar neutrinos to test the NSI resolution of this tension and to break these degeneracies. Using recent solar neutrino data from LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, we show that dark matter direct detection experiments already constrain part of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension. These experiments can also probe parts of the NSI parameter space that even DUNE will be blind to. Our analysis combines nuclear recoils from $^8$B neutrinos and electron recoils from $pp$ neutrinos. A future xenon experiment, such as XLZD or PandaX-xT, will be able to cover a significant fraction of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension.

papers.title: Measuring $V_{cb}$ at electron-proton colliders
papers.abstract: We study the prospects for an independent determination of $V_{cb}$ from bottom-tagged charged-current deep-inelastic scattering at future electron-proton colliders: the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh. The transition $e^- c \to ν_e b$ probes $|V_{cb}|^2$ through a process with different theoretical and experimental uncertainties from semileptonic $B$ decays. We fit ratios of $b$-tagged charged-current event counts over flavour-inclusive ones in kinematic bins, including correlated parton-distribution and flavour-tag calibration uncertainties, and floating the other CKM parameters. With projected parton distributions and tagging performance motivated by existing studies, we find a potential relative sensitivity in $|V_{cb}|$ of about $0.8\%$ at the LHeC with $1\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity and $0.7\%$ at FCC-eh with $2\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$. The corresponding EIC sensitivity is instead at the level of $20 - 30 \%$, depending on the configuration. The LHeC could thus provide a high-energy determination competitive with low-energy ones, but with substantially different dominant systematic uncertainties, on the timescale of its proposed operation between the HL-LHC and FCC-ee. We identify precise flavour-tag calibration and control of the kinematic response as the main requirements for realising this potential sensitivity.

papers.title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy Without a Phase Reference
papers.abstract: Stabilizer Rényi entropy quantifies magic relative to a complete Pauli frame. In settings such as helicity states of massless particles, unsynchronized qubit registers, energy eigenbases, and systems under superselection rules, the computational basis may be fixed while the transverse Pauli axes remain unspecified. The stabilizer Rényi entropy then depends on the choice of those axes. We define a phase-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy by averaging the Pauli moments before taking the logarithm. It is exactly invariant under independent local rephasings. For pure states, it vanishes precisely when the state is a stabilizer state in every phase convention. For a broad class of sparse supports, it reduces to a closed-form function of the basis-state probabilities alone. Within this class, the ceiling for $n$ channels is $\ln[n^{3}/(6n-5)]$ for $n\geq3$ and $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ for two channels. We apply the invariant to tree-level gluon scattering at four and five points, where the helicity-basis phases are unspecified. It saturates the two- and three-channel ceilings: $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ at four points and $\ln\frac{27}{13}$ in $3\to2$ scattering. In same-helicity $2\to3$ scattering, it lies between a floor of $\ln\frac{8}{7}$ and a ceiling of $\ln\frac{184}{125}$, reached in the resolved soft limit and particular collinear limits, respectively. In every configuration studied, the invariant is independent of the fixed external colors.

papers.title: A 4D $T^\prime$-expanded lattice QCD equation of state with a multi-dimensional 3D-Ising-type critical contribution
papers.abstract: Inferring the possible existence and location of a critical point on the QCD phase diagram through experimental observations requires equations of state that include both lattice QCD constraints and critical behavior. In this manuscript, we present the first four-dimensional equation of state in the $(T,μ_B,μ_Q,μ_S)$ space combining the lattice 4D $T^\prime$-Expansion Scheme with a critical contribution mapped from the 3D Ising model. We extend the earlier two-dimensional construction, the so-called Ising 2D-TExS in the $(T, μ_B)$ plane, promoting the critical point to a parametrizable critical surface in the full four-dimensional thermodynamic space. Our framework provides a family of equations of state to systematically study the effects of criticality in realistic hydrodynamic simulations with $BQS$ conserved charges, going beyond the case of strangeness neutrality, by varying the geometry of the critical surface and the strength of criticality at finite $μ_B$, $μ_Q$ and $μ_S$ separately.

papers.title: Exact two-loop gravitational tail integrals and their ultraviolet-infrared structure
papers.abstract: Gravitational tail-of-tail corrections arise when radiation scatters twice from the mass-monopole field of its source. In the multipolar effective field theory, one of the two-loop topologies contributing to this process involves genuinely coupled loop momenta, preventing its evaluation through nested one-loop integrations. After tensor reduction, this nonfactorizing structure leads to a particularly challenging family of scalar integrals with unbounded numerator powers as the multipole rank increases. We derive exact closed-form expressions for the entire relevant integer numerator domain, valid in generic dimension and accommodating Feynman, retarded, and advanced prescriptions through consistent analytic continuation. Near $d=3+ε$, we also obtain explicit Laurent expansions through $O(ε)$, retaining the subleading information needed in higher-order radiative calculations. While these expansions determine the dimensional poles, identifying their ultraviolet (UV) or infrared (IR) origin requires a separate analysis of momentum regions. We carry out this analysis throughout the integral domain and apply it directly to the coupled tail-of-tail emission diagram for arbitrary electric and magnetic multipoles. In this way, we independently determine the UV and IR residues, and explicitly verify that the complete infrared pole structure, including both double and simple poles, agrees with the exponentiation of the one-loop gravitational tail. The UV residues, calculated directly from hard-momentum regions, reproduce the established multipole anomalous dimensions when combined with the known contributions of the remaining diagrams.

papers.title: Virtual photon bremsstrahlung in a magnetized quark-gluon-plasma
papers.abstract: We investigate dilepton production via virtual quark bremsstrahlung in a hot, magnetized quark-gluon plasma (QGP), extending the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) framework to account for a background magnetic field and for Fermi-Dirac quark statistics. An external electromagnetic field drives the quark distribution out of equilibrium, and this off-equilibrium correction, obtained from the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation, is in principle explicit in the electric and magnetic field strengths. We argue that this correction, being linear in the electric field, vanishes identically upon integration over the full dilepton solid angle and therefore does not contribute to the dilepton production rate (DPR). The leading magnetic-field signature in the rate instead enters entirely through the equilibrium sector: the medium density and Debye screening mass, computed from the Landau-level structure of the magnetized QGP, modifying the LPM suppression parameter. Working in the regime relevant to the hydrodynamic phase of heavy-ion collisions, we present the LPM-induced DPR for quark scatterers and establish, for the first time, a nonzero magnetic-field imprint on this observable through the LPM mechanism.

papers.title: Multiboson production at multi-TeV lepton colliders as complementary probes to rare Higgs decays
papers.abstract: We study the potential of very high-energy lepton colliders to probe effective operators affecting the loop-induced Higgs boson decays $h\to γγ$ and $h\to Zγ$, providing constraints complementary to Higgs coupling measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. In particular, we consider processes with two and three bosons in the final state and analyze their individual and combined impact on the effective field theory parameter space. We demonstrate that these processes at a multi-TeV lepton collider can improve the bounds from rare Higgs decays and electroweak precision observables, surpassing the projections for High-Luminosity LHC and FCC-ee. This is especially true for triboson processes, whose sensitivity is enhanced by the growth with energy of the new physics cross-sections, making them the dominant constraint at very high energies, potentially competitive with FCC-hh.

papers.title: Probing the proton structure with minimum bias and low-pt dimuon events at hadron colliders
papers.abstract: This paper presents two methods for probing the proton structure and the number of partonic interactions in proton-proton collisions using dimuon production and minimum bias events. At the LHC these targeted measurements can provide information on the average number of partonic scatters in different event classes, their dependence on the partonic momentum fraction, x, and potentially partonic flavour. Within a simple mostly geometric model of multiparton interactions as quasi-independent scatters, the measurements can be used to make inference about the proton-proton overlap dependence on impact parameter and its partonic-x dependence.

papers.title: Shear viscosity from fluctuations in linearized relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: In this work we incorporate thermal fluctuations into fluid-dynamic simulations with the vHLLE code, in linear approximation. The fluctuations are built in following the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The effect of space discretization into cells in numerical hydrodynamics on the spatial correlation of fluctuations is studied with the help of static structure factor. A difference from the continuum result is pointed out and systematically investigated. Time evolution of the ensuing fluctuations is examined and the Green-Kubo formula is used for the extraction of shear viscosity from the fluctuations. The extracted value is demonstrated to be the same as the input value of the shear viscosity for the simulations using Israel-Stewart equations. It is also shown that numerical regulators commonly used in the codes to ensure stability of the calculation severely spoil the fluctuations and break the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

papers.title: Deviations to cobimaximal mixing in a 3+1 neutrino scenario
papers.abstract: Cobimaximal mixing remains a viable approximate pattern since the predicted atmospheric angle ($π/4$) and Dirac CP phase ($-π/2$) are compatible with current experimental data at the $3σ$ level. In this work, we investigate how an additional sterile neutrino state breaks the cobimaximal mixing and the underlying $μ-τ$ reflection symmetry in a $3+1$ neutrino scenario. Given the strong constraints already imposed on active-sterile mixings, we examine the resulting restrictions on the model parameter space, assuming a small symmetry breaking induced by the sterile state. We derive predictions for the relevant model parameters, active-sterile mixing angles, and Dirac CP-violating phases, by considering small deviations from the symmetric limit. We also analyze the allowed combinations of Majorana phases through their impact on the effective Majorana mass governing neutrinoless double beta decay. Current experimental limits on this process impose severe constraints on the inverted ordering realization of the $3+1$ scenario, excluding the small breaking regime within the parameter ranges considered. In contrast, the normal ordering case remains viable and predicts values of the effective Majorana mass that lie within the sensitivity reach of upcoming neutrinoless double beta decay experiments.

papers.title: HEPTABench: A framework for portable and controlled agentic evaluations in high energy physics
papers.abstract: Quantifying the capability and reliability of agentic systems in high-energy physics (HEP) requires repeated evaluations under controlled configurations. Establishing whether changes to models, tools, or harnesses improve performance also requires these components to be varied independently. We present the High Energy Physics Tool-and-Agent Benchmarking (HEPTABench) framework for portable and controlled evaluations of agentic systems, with separately configurable tasks, scaffolding, models, providers, harnesses, and domain capabilities. The framework combines HEP benchmark tasks and scientific rubrics with experiment execution and versioned tool interfaces. To support inspection, reproducibility, and post-hoc grading, the framework prioritizes recording and reporting complete experiment specifications, agent trajectories, and experiment artifacts. We demonstrate the framework in two benchmark campaigns. The first campaign evaluates a forward long-lived-particle reach calculation across four frontier coding-agent systems, comparing their built-in coding tools with the same tools supplemented by HEP domain tools. We show that including these HEP domain tools improves numerical accuracy and reduces trial-to-trial dispersion for every tested system. In a complementary campaign covering eight symbolic two-body decay tasks, we show that adding symbolic domain tools increases the fraction of successful trials for Claude Haiku 4.5 from $8\%$ to $79\%$, while GPT-5.5 succeeds in every trial with built-in tools alone. Through systematic evaluation of agentic systems, HEPTABench enables the identification of factors that improve the accuracy and reliability of their scientific work.

papers.title: Cosmological Consequences of a Highly Decoupled Right-handed Neutrino
papers.abstract: In the minimal type-I seesaw, one right-handed neutrino (RHN) can decouple from neutrino mass generation. Such a state is usually neglected, yet its feeble couplings make it long-lived, and it can dominate the energy density of the Universe before decaying. We study this in a minimal $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, where the RHNs are produced through $B-L$ gauge interactions, for the cases of a decoupled lightest RHN $N_1$ and a decoupled heaviest RHN $N_3$. The resulting early matter-dominated era dilutes the baryon asymmetry, and for decoupled $N_3$ it also delays the equilibration of the charged-lepton Yukawa interactions, allowing a lighter $N_1$ to generate the asymmetry in the unflavoured regime. Breaking $U(1)_{B-L}$ forms cosmic strings whose gravitational-wave background acquires a spectral break from the early matter-dominated era, with a frequency set by the decoupled RHN mass and the lightest neutrino mass, within reach of future detectors such as SKA, THEIA, LISA, $μ$ARES, DECIGO and ET.

papers.title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of Lévy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional Lévy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(ρ)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(ρ_{\rm out},ρ_{\rm side},ρ_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic Lévy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
papers.abstract: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4σ$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $μ{\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

papers.title: Color Lorentz force on a transversely polarized quark in the nucleon
papers.abstract: The $x^2$ moment of the genuine twist-3 component of the unpolarized scalar parton distribution function $e(x)$ is related to the average transverse color Lorentz force experienced by a transversely polarized quark in an unpolarized nucleon. This higher-twist quantity probes quark--gluon correlations and provides unique insight into the nonperturbative dynamics of quantum chromodynamics. For the first time, we study the corresponding off-forward matrix element and derive its Lorentz-covariant decomposition in terms of generalized form factors. We calculate these form factors from light-front wave functions obtained by solving the light-front Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework. Their Fourier transforms provide a spatial picture of the transverse color forces in impact-parameter space. In particular, $\mathscr{F}_2$, whose forward limit is directly related to the twist-3 matrix element $e_2$, can be interpreted as the impact-parameter-space representation of the Boer--Mulders force, providing an intuitive spatial picture of the final-state interaction mechanism underlying the Boer--Mulders effect.

papers.title: Covariant approach to allowed beta decay
papers.abstract: We propose a Lorentz-covariant on-shell formalism for allowed nuclear beta decay. Nuclear matrix elements are organized in a systematic effective field theory expansion in the recoil momentum, with the dependence on nuclear spin and polarization encoded in little-group-covariant structures. In this language, we construct the most general standard and exotic currents for allowed transitions through first recoil order. We then derive the differential decay distribution encoded in a set of Lorentz-invariant form factors. Specializing to the rest frame of the parent nucleus, we relate our parameters to those used in the traditional beta-decay literature and in nucleon- and quark-level effective field theories. The formalism provides a natural framework for extensions to higher recoil orders, radiative corrections, and forbidden transitions.

papers.title: One-loop contributing for $A \rightarrow Z Z γ$ in the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model with Vector-Like Quarks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present the first results for the one-loop decay $A \rightarrow ZZγ$ in the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model and its extension with Vector-Like Quarks. We calculate the one-loop partial decay widths and branching ratios for both unpolarized and polarized final-state $Z$ bosons. The effects of Vector-Like Quarks propagating in the loop are also examined in our phenomenological analysis. We find that the branching ratios can reach $10^{-5}-10^{-4}$ for several benchmark points within the viable parameter space of the considered models. The contributions from Vector-Like Quarks can modify the total rates by approximately $5\%$. With the high luminosities expected at future multi-TeV muon colliders, these effects may be experimentally accessible.

papers.title: Heavy flavour production in the presence of a weak magnetic field
papers.abstract: We calculate analytic expression for the cross section up to order $(eB)^2$ for the production of a heavy quark $(Q)$ of mass $m_Q$ through the gluon $(g)$ fusion process $g+g\to Q+\bar{Q}$ in the presence of a constant weak external magnetic field $(B)$ with strength $eB \ll m_Q^2$. This is done using the weak-field expansion of the fermion propagator calculated within Schwinger's proper-time formalism. Owing to the hierarchy of scales ($m_Q^2 \gg eB$), we neglect the effects of the magnetic field on the quark and antiquark spinors in the external lines. Since the magnetic field breaks rotational invariance, the cross section becomes anisotropic and depends on the relative orientation angle $(θ)$ between the magnetic field and the incoming gluons in the center-of-mass frame. The lowest-order magnetic correction to the vacuum cross section scales as $(eB)^2$ and is found to have $\cos 2θ$ and $\cos 4θ$ dependence, reflecting the breaking of rotational symmetry by the magnetic field. The cross section is maximized when the gluons propagate along the field direction ($θ= 0, π$) and minimized in the perpendicular configuration ($θ= π/2$). The resulting asymmetry peaks near the production threshold and falls with increasing center-of-mass energy, scaling as $(eB)^2/m_Q^4$ with the quark mass. These results provide direct, calculable signatures of the initial-stage magnetic field in relativistic heavy-ion collisions which can, in principle, be imprinted on heavy-flavour observables measured in the final state of heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: A mechanism of the power-counting breaking in chiral perturbation theory
papers.abstract: Chiral perturbation theory is a power tool for studying the low-energy strong interactions. In the conventional chiral expansion, according to the power counting rule, the higher-order corrections for physical observables are expected to decrease order by order as the chiral dimension increases. However, most previous study of $πK$ scattering lengths by different references showed that the $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ correction to the scattering lengths is anomalously large and even exceeds the $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ one. It poses a serious challenge to the convergence of chiral expansion. In order to explore the underlying origin of this phenomenon, the contributions of two-loop diagrams, one-loop diagrams and tree diagrams for the $πK$ scattering amplitude are detailed analyzed. The reducible two-loop integrals, sunset integrals and vertex integrals from the $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ order all violate the power counting rule. The sunset and vertex integrals can be largely canceled numerically, but not enough. Furthermore, $πK$ scattering is compared with $ππ$ scattering, which seems not violate the power counting rule. The analysis indicates that $ππ$ scattering contains a higher symmetry, although each $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$-order part also violates the power counting rule, but the violation is much smaller than the one from $πK$ scattering. Large kaon mass also makes a contribution to the power-counting breaking, but it is not a major origin. Hence, it needs to pay more attention to the many-loop low-symmetry diagrams in future work. These diagrams may give large contribution and cannot be ignored.

papers.title: Octupole parton structure of spin-3/2 targets
papers.abstract: In spin-$3/2$ targets, octupole polarization can reveal quark and gluon correlations beyond those probed by vector polarization and quadrupole alignment. Here, we construct the complete leading-twist gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distribution basis, with 32 independent coefficients for each specified Wilson-line and color structure. Fourteen of these describe octupole dependence in gluon number, helicity, and linear polarization. In heavy-quark-pair leptoproduction at small, nonzero pair imbalance, comparing target states with opposite octupoles and identical lower moments isolates the octupole contribution. Beam-helicity reversal and joint angular projections in target orientation and pair-imbalance azimuth can then separate all fourteen gluon octupole responses at leading-power Born order. We also derive the incoming-target quark responses in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan production. Time-reversal relations between distributions remain valid under symmetry-preserving renormalization and evolution, while predictions across processes require factorization formulas connecting those distributions to scattering observables. Finally, we connect this framework to polarized $^{7}$Li through its collinear limits and nuclear spin-orbital correlations.

papers.title: Kernel moments and thermodynamic stability in nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio models
papers.abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. At fixed couplings and kernel, every admissible positive Gaussian mixture develops negative total entropy at sufficiently large source mass for each fixed positive temperature. In a separate light-source fit to pion observables and a subtracted condensate, one quartic-exponent kernel has positive entropy and heat capacity for all $T>0$, while $dP/dε=s/C_V$ exceeds unity on a finite interval. This constructive example separates thermal positivity from the static EOS slope test. Numerical refits show that the enhancement weakens with the condensate input, and a certified counterexample excludes uniform thermal positivity over the adopted matching domain. The results provide diagnostics of the mean-field functional, rather than a preferred phenomenological kernel. Omitted thermal mesons can change the low-temperature slope test, and the static derivative does not determine a real-time front velocity.

papers.title: Parton and nuclear dynamics at large $x$: the CJ26 global QCD analysis
papers.abstract: We present the new CTEQ-JLab global QCD analysis, called CJ26, that simultaneously fits parton distribution functions of the proton and nuclear effects in deuteron targets. This work includes, for the first time in a global fit, the full set of JLab 6 GeV inclusive DIS measurements and the first published JLab 12 GeV data. The analysis focuses on the large-$x$ region, and carefully treats the interplay between higher-twist effects and off-shell corrections in low-energy proton and deuteron target data. We discuss their effect on quark and gluon distributions, and highlight the importance of quantifying the experimental correlated systematic uncertainty to achieve fits of the highest accuracy. We also outline how upcoming data may help unravel the nuclear and partonic dynamics in light nuclei. The extracted next-to-leading order parton distributions are available on the CJ web pages in LHAPDF format for general use, accompanied by leading- and higher-twist structure functions calculated with the simultaneously fitted PDFs, higher-twist corrections, and off-shell corrections. This write up clarifies several points that became clearer while finalizing the CJ26 paper and can be read as a companion to the latter.

papers.title: QGrAT: Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer for Jet Tagging
papers.abstract: Lorentz symmetry and the three-prong structure of hadronic top decays provide physical guidance for designing compact quantum jet taggers. We introduce QGrAT (Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer), a quantum transformer that incorporates these structures into its interactions between constituent qubits. Geometric features constructed from the constituent four-momenta are organised by the grades of the spacetime Clifford algebra $C\ell(1,3)$, and their grade-specific inner products determine the pairwise attention couplings. For fixed constituents and co-transforming reference vectors, these couplings are Lorentz invariant, although the component-wise input encoding makes the complete classifier frame dependent. An auxiliary qubit introduces an explicit three-particle interaction through products of pairwise Minkowski inner products, while a trainable in-circuit readout converts the resulting quantum state into a classification score. We evaluate the architecture in state-vector simulation on the Top Tagging benchmarks. With ten constituents per jet, the configuration using grades $0\text{-}3$ and the three-particle ancilla requires twelve qubits and $144$ trainable parameters, reaching AUC $0.944 \pm 0.002$ and background rejection $1/\varepsilon_B = 35.7 \pm 2.4\ (96.8 \pm 7.7)$ at signal efficiency $\varepsilon_S = 0.50\ (0.30)$. This performance is competitive with the L-GATr-Slim baseline at matched constituent and parameter budgets. Adding the three-particle ancilla raises background rejection at $50\%$ signal efficiency from $19.9$ to $35.7$, whereas extending the representation to the tested grade-$4$ feature gives no consistent improvement. The study establishes a framework for incorporating spacetime geometry into quantum attention and identifies explicit three-particle correlations as the principal source of improved background rejection among the architectural variations tested.

papers.title: Non-accumulation of background-enhanced neutrino forces in proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: In a neutrino background, the vacuum two-neutrino exchange potential $V \propto G_F^2 /r^5$ acts as a much longer-ranged interaction, scaling as $V\sim1/r$ for a directional background. A proto-neutron star (PNS) hosts one of the densest astrophysical neutrino environments known, and naturally provides a setting in which to test whether this pairwise enhancement produces a macroscopic Hartree contribution. We show that this does not happen. In the spin-independent sector, averaging over pair orientations projects the background onto its angular monopole. The bulk Hartree contribution then saturates instead of growing with system size. We also find that the spin-dependent parity-conserving and parity-violating terms do not generate macroscopic growth under the PNS mean-field conditions considered here. Thus, although the pair potential can be strongly enhanced, the resulting bulk interaction remains very small. The suppression comes from the angular and oscillatory structure of the kernel, not from screening. Within the Standard Model mechanism considered here, the effect is not important for the PNS equation of state or for events like pulsar kicks.

papers.title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
papers.abstract: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $τ$ and $μ$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8σ$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3σ$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.

papers.title: Neutrino Tridents and $W$-boson production at the Muon Collider
papers.abstract: Muon colliders are exceptionally intense sources of multi-TeV neutrinos, allowing even relatively small detectors to record large rates of neutrino interactions. In addition to serving as neutrino-ion collider for precision measurements of neutrino deep inelastic scattering, this setup allow to study even rare neutrino processes with at high statistics. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of measuring neutrino trident and on-shell W-boson production, predicting over one million trident events and one hundred thousand W-boson events in a 100 kg silicon-based active target over ten years and allowing to detect these processes for the first time. We further show that these measurements could constrain new vector and axial-vector interactions beyond projected DUNE sensitivities and provide unprecedented constraints on the high-x photon distribution through W-boson production near threshold. We also discuss strategies for signal-background discrimination and the resulting detector requirements.

papers.title: What Do Event Generators Compute? Flux Functionals from Detector Operators
papers.abstract: Every physical prediction of an event generator is a statement about the hadronic fluxes that can be recorded by particle detectors. By contrast, the formal backbone of modern event-generator precision is provided by the unobservable partonic final states of the parton shower, with hadronisation included as a model. We construct the probability distribution of the hadronic fluxes non-perturbatively, directly from detector operators acting on asymptotic hadronic states, and encode it in an event generator source functional. This distribution contains every measurement a detector can make, and is therefore what a generator must compute with precision, including the effects of hadronisation. Restricting the functional to the energy flow yields the parton shower source functional, which is infrared and collinear safe and contains every calorimetric observable, making it a natural object against which to assess parton-shower accuracy. We compute its logarithmic structure at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, finding it directly sensitive to kinematic recoil and hence to the recoil scheme of a parton shower. The parton shower functional depends on a continuum of low scales, one for each resolved direction, and in a toy model its logarithms cannot be entirely resummed within a factorisation whose evolution derives only from the high-scale physics. Our operator-based formulation opens the door to the study of event-generator-like systems in theories beyond QCD, including conformal theories such as $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and thereby offers a new route to non-perturbative insight into event generation.

papers.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
papers.abstract: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential.
