After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.

papers.title: Dark Matter Stability from residual flavour symmetries
papers.abstract: We propose a model-independent framework in which Dark Matter stability emerges naturally from residual discrete $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries left unbroken by the spontaneous breaking of continuous flavour symmetries, both Abelian and non-Abelian. No ad hoc stabilizing symmetry is required, as Dark Matter stability is an inherent consequence of the underlying flavour dynamics. As an explicit example, we construct a prototype model based on a $\text{SU}(2)_\text{F} \otimes \text{U}(1)_\text{F}$ Froggatt-Nielsen symmetry, which successfully reproduces the observed charged lepton mass spectrum and the PMNS mixing matrix, while identifying the lightest sterile neutrino as a stable Dark Matter candidate. Furthermore, we study the Dark Matter phenomenology within our model in the freeze-in regime, including production channels mediated by higher-dimensional operators suppressed by the cutoff scale $Λ$. Our analysis shows that continuous flavour symmetries can provide a unified, self-consistent framework addressing both the flavour puzzle and the origin, stability, and production of Dark Matter.

papers.title: Implications for new physics solutions to the LSND and MiniBooNE anomalies after MicroBooNE results
papers.abstract: Over the past couple of decades, the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector (LSND) and MiniBooNE (MB) neutrino experiments have provided statistically significant evidence of persistent and as yet unexplained electron-like event excesses. The MicroBooNE experiment, with sensitive particle identification capabilities designed to shed light on these anomalous results, has conducted a number of analyses to test whether the excess is due to photons, electrons or $e^+e^-$ pair productions, all of which give almost identical signals in LSND and MB. Recent MicroBooNE searches, in addition to checking Standard Model (SM) processes, have focused on proposed new physics scenarios involving new mediators and dark portals beyond the SM. We study the consequences and effects of these analyses for the many theoretical proposals put forth to generate the three types of signals above in order to understand the observed excesses. We discuss which classes of solutions are allowed, disallowed or require further scrutiny involving theoretical and experimental efforts. We give an example of a new solution that survives the restrictions imposed by MicroBooNE results and other existing bounds. We point out that a light ($m\leq 30$ MeV) dark neutral spin zero mediator with dominantly pseudoscalar couplings, decaying to an $e^+e^-$ pair, can account for the observations. We indicate that if such a model is realised, it may point to the possibility that neutrinos are Dirac particles, and that there are dark Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) of mass ${\cal O}(100)$ MeV. We discuss issues related to CP violation and ultra-violet completion of these models. Finally we stress that a search for the excess in incoherent scattering channels in MicroBooNE and SBND could help clarify the physics behind these persistent anomalies.

papers.title: MadNIS, Ready for Production at LO
papers.abstract: We extend neural multi-channel importance sampling in MadNIS to full proton-proton processes in a production-ready event-generation setup. We benchmark a wide range of LHC processes, including multi-jet, vector-boson, top-quark, and Higgs production, and obtain event-generation speed-ups of up to a factor of 250 without process-specific hyperparameter tuning. We quantify how the speed-up scales with training time and final-state multiplicity, and when the training cost amortizes. MadNIS will become the default for phase-space integration and event generation at leading order in MadGraph.

papers.title: Charged Lepton Flavor Violation: A Theory Overview
papers.abstract: We present a theory-oriented overview of the significance of charged-lepton flavor violation -- one of the cleanest windows onto physics beyond the Standard Model. We also summarize the current experimental landscape and illustrate how different measurements can diagnose the underlying new physics.

papers.title: Decay-Assisted Leptogenesis during Preheating
papers.abstract: We revisit the non-thermal leptogenesis mechanism during preheating using the quantum Boltzmann equations. This framework allows us to study the production and decay of heavy right-handed neutrinos in a consistent manner. Due to their fermionic nature, right-handed neutrino production can saturate after a few inflaton oscillations when their occupation numbers approach unity. Right-handed neutrino decays can deplete their occupation numbers, allowing more particles to be produced and generating a larger lepton asymmetry. Compared with the case where right-handed neutrinos decay only after production has finished, we find that the final baryon asymmetry can be enhanced by two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Vortex structures in momentum distributions from multi-pair production
papers.abstract: The vortex structures in the momentum distributions of multiple particle-antiparticle pairs produced from the vacuum by a spatially uniform, time-varying electric field with arbitrary polarization are investigated using the Bogoliubov transformation. For linearly polarized fields, as the field strength increases, the nodal lines in the multi-pair momentum distribution break up into vortex-antivortex pairs in both the bosonic and fermionic cases. Each vortex carries a topological charge that is an integer multiple of the single-pair vortex topological charge. For circular polarization, a central vortex appears at all field strengths. For bosons, its topological charge is an integer multiple of the single-pair vortex topological charge; for fermions, it is an integer multiple of the vortex topological charge for single-pair production with zero total spin projection along the field propagation direction. For elliptical polarization with suitable ellipticity, discrete vortices coexist with a central vortex. In this case, however, the integer-multiple relation for fermions generally fails because the two-pair production amplitude is a determinant and spin-channel contributions are separated in momentum space. These results provide a theoretical basis for understanding the vortex topology of multi-pair production in strong-field QED and for its potential control.

papers.title: Impact of Window Observables on the Transversity Quark Parton Distribution Function
papers.abstract: We study the potential impact of lattice QCD window observables on nucleon isovector quark transversity parton distribution functions (PDFs) using the ePump Hessian-updating framework. Window observables, recently proposed in arXiv:2505.22795 as benchmark quantities enabling direct quantitative comparison between lattice QCD and phenomenological PDF extractions, are weighted integrals of PDFs over a range of Bjorken-$x$ for which both approaches are reliable. Experimental determinations of transversity PDFs carry uncertainties of 50--100%, while current lattice calculations have achieved comparable or better precision, creating an opportunity for lattice inputs to significantly constrain a global analysis. We evaluate the constraining power of existing lattice QCD computations of transversity window moments and Gaussian windows against current phenomenological PDF. We additionally examine prospective tensor charges in the transversity channel and estimate the PDF uncertainty reduction achievable at current and near-future lattice precision. Our results provide quantitative guidance on which window observables will most constrain global PDF analyses.

papers.title: Invisible Decays of the $Z$ in Portal Matter Models at Tera-Z
papers.abstract: Searches for new contributions to the invisible width of the $Z$, $ΔΓ_{inv}$, can be used to provide model-dependent constraints on new physics that may arise from an unknown dark sector. In the vector portal setup considered here it is shown that loops of portal matter (PM) fields, having both Standard Model (SM) and dark sector quantum numbers, can lead to new contributions to $ΔΓ_{inv}$ that satisfy current experimental constraints while being simultaneously accessible to measurements at the future Tera-Z. Such PM fields, which here take the form of vector-like fermions, are well known to be able to induce kinetic mixing (KM) between the SM and dark photons (DP) at low energies. This analysis is performed within a simplified version of a previously examined `$E_6-$like' setup that predicts a calculable value for the strength of KM in a phenomenologically interesting range. On the other hand, owing to the constraint on the invisible branching fraction of the Higgs, the tree-level mixing of the SM and a weak isosinglet dark Higgs fields yields a value of $ΔΓ_{inv}$ which is far too small to be observable. A similar result holds for the shift in the $Z$'s invisible width induced by the mass and/or KM of the $Z$ with the light DP which then subsequently decays to dark matter. On the other hand, PM models wherein the light dark Higgs carries a significant admixture of a $T_3\neq 0$ weak isospin component are shown to already violate existing $ΔΓ_{inv}$ constraints in the absence of parameter tuning. Future measurements of $ΔΓ_{inv}$ can thus play an important role in providing indirect constraints on dark sector interactions and PM model building, in particular, on PM loops not necessarily associated with the generation of KM of the DP with the corresponding SM field.

papers.title: Chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons: Mass relations and decay predictions after the 2026 LHCb discoveries
papers.abstract: Three spectacular LHCb measurements in 2026---the observations of $Ω_{cc}^{+}$, $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$, and the beauty-strange structure $B_{s0}^{*}(5700)^0$---make possible an experimentally constrained analysis of chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons. The doubly charmed masses test the earlier Ma--Harada prediction and support a compact, internally S-wave $cc$ color source. We combine this comparison with the heavy-quark--diquark hyperfine relation and with chiral gaps from the theory of chiral doublers, to construct consistent $ccs$ and $bbs$ parity multiplets and a conditional extension to $bcs$. Under meson-to-baryon parity-gap transfer, the $349$ MeV input from the $D_s$ sector gives negative-parity $ccs$ targets near $4.075$ and $4.183$ GeV. The separate $332$ MeV input from the $B_s$ sector fixes the $bbs$ partner masses relative to their unknown ground-state mass, conditional on the new beauty-strange state's chiral-partner assignment. We relate the differences of hyperfine splittings in the two parity sectors of mesons and baryons, and identify equal reduced single-pion widths, an E1 reduced-width ratio $1:8:4:5$, and a kaon selection rule whose leading predictions contain no new transition parameters. Absolute widths are estimated by matching the published Bardeen--Eichten--Hill and Harada--Rho--Sasaki meson calculations to a common convention. In the reference calculation, all members of the predicted $ccs$ and $bbs$ multiplets are narrow. In the proposed $Ω_{QQ}π^0$ and $Ω_{QQ}γ$ searches at LHCb, these states are expected to produce peaks dominated by detector resolution, allowing their masses and decay patterns to be investigated even when their intrinsic widths remain unresolved. The upper charm state is above kaon threshold but protected in the spectator limit.

papers.title: Event Generation for Neutrino and Muon DIS at the LHC
papers.abstract: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. Realising this potential requires accurate and precise simulations of neutral- and charged-current DIS. We systematically compare the predictions of NLO general-purpose Monte Carlo (MC) event generators for neutrino- and muon-initiated DIS at the LHC (Sherpa, Herwig7, and POWHEG) against analytical structure-function calculations (YADISM) and dedicated neutrino simulation packages (GENIE, NuWro, GiBUU). Within this framework, we quantify the role of higher-order QCD corrections, (nuclear) parton distribution functions (PDFs), parton shower and hadronisation modelling, and QED radiation both for inclusive observables and for the FASER fiducial selections. We also present representative applications to the FASER neutrino programme: comparisons with its most recent data from the emulsion and electronic sub-detectors, a study of strange PDF sensitivity in the dimuon final state, and predictions for charged-hadron production in semi-inclusive DIS. Our analysis highlights the agreement of modern event generators for inclusive and differential DIS observables once common settings are adopted, while differences remain for observables sensitive to the hadronic final state.

papers.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
papers.abstract: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.

papers.title: Two-pion source analysis in small to large systems at SPS energies
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, femtoscopic measurements using Lévy-stable source functions have been carried out in collision systems ranging from small to large at SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies. In recent years, these have been accompanied by a number of phenomenological studies of the same systems and energies. We contribute to this line of work by investigating the shape of two-pion pair-source distributions in central $^7$Be+$^9$Be and $^{129}$Xe+$^{139}$La collisions simulated with the UrQMD model in cascade mode. To make the comparison with measurements meaningful, kinematic selections similar to the experimental ones are applied to the simulated events and particles. One-dimensional Lévy fits are performed, and the resulting source parameters are studied as functions of pair transverse mass, collision energy, and system size. We find that the simulated sources are well described by Lévy distributions in all systems considered, which offers a common phenomenological picture of the space-time structure of pion emission. Finally, we compare our findings with results from an intermediate system, Ar+Sc. The results serve as a purely hadronic reference for past and upcoming femtoscopic measurements of the NA61/SHINE experiment.

papers.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
papers.abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
papers.abstract: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

papers.title: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
papers.abstract: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. The predicted momentum spectra at approximately 0 and 75 degrees are compared with experimental measurements of the atmospheric muon flux and with commonly used analytic parametrizations. The two interaction-model configurations give similar spectra and describe the principal momentum and zenith-angle dependences of the data. The agent independently reconstructs the same observable through a different sampling strategy and keeps every steering card, executable, seed, log, and analysis script bound to the result it produced; its output is consistent with the direct calculation at the level resolved by the present comparison. Transferred to Mars, the workflow reproduces the CORSIKA 8 benchmark, and transferred to Venus it produces the first prediction of the surface muon flux, an environment for which no measurement exists. The agent thus extends the workflow from auditable reproduction to first-principles prediction: it autonomously reconfigures the simulation(atmosphere, magnetic field, electric field)for new environments, while the proton-only primary model, limited high-momentum statistics, and an incomplete systematic-uncertainty treatment bound the physical precision that can currently be claimed.

papers.title: Parton distribution functions and strong coupling constant: MSHT
papers.abstract: We present an overview of the MSHT family of global PDF fits. We describe the underlying methodology, including parameterisation choice, theoretical inputs and datasets included in the fit. We describe the impact of recent theoretical advances in the inclusion of higher order QCD and EW corrections on the fit and their implications for phenomenology. We discuss recent methodological improvements and ongoing studies relating to closure tests of the parameterisation flexibility and the inclusion of errors on errors for experimental data. We in addition discuss recent results on the determination of the strong coupling from the MSHT fits.

papers.title: Concurrence Dynamics in Self-Gravitating Mixed Neutrinos
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement generated by Newtonian self-gravity in a two-particle system of mixed neutrinos and quantify it by means of the concurrence. Starting from the gravitational coupling between the mass operators, we show that the two-particle Hamiltonian splits into local single-particle terms and an effective Ising interaction in the mass basis, the latter being solely responsible for the generation of correlations. For initially separable flavor states the concurrence is obtained in closed analytic form: it oscillates between zero and a maximum fixed by the mixing angle alone, while the gravitational coupling sets the recurrence time. We further establish a one-to-one correspondence between the concurrence and the reduced-state purity previously derived for this model, thus providing an independent quantum-information description of the same gravitationally induced correlations. Finally, we show that the concurrence does not depend on the Majorana phase, so that Dirac and Majorana parametrizations yield identical entanglement dynamics. These results isolate the genuinely entangling sector of the gravitational evolution and provide a compact analytic characterization of gravity-induced quantum correlations in mixed neutrino systems.

papers.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
papers.abstract: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $Λ$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $η(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = α{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $Λ$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $Λ$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $Ω_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $η(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $η(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $α\simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.

papers.title: Probing first-generation doublet vector-like leptons via single production at the 3 TeV CLIC
papers.abstract: The single production of first-generation $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ doublet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) with $\sqrt{s}=3~\mathrm{TeV}$ is studied. The neutral and charged VLL states are investigated through $e^+e^-\rightarrowν_e\bar N+\barν_eN$ and $e^+e^-\rightarrow e^\pm E^\mp$, respectively. The neutral VLL is searched for in the $N\rightarrow W^\mp e^\pm$ channel with $W^\pm\rightarrow jj$, leading to the $e^\pm+2j+\slashed{E}_T$ final state. The charged VLL is explored through $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm h$ ($h\rightarrow b\bar b$) and $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm Z$ ($Z\rightarrow q\bar q$), yielding the $e^+e^-+2b$ and $e^+e^-+2j$ signatures. Signal and background simulations include initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, and detector effects. Cut-based analyses are performed for integrated luminosities of $1$, $3$, and $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ to obtain the exclusion and discovery sensitivities in the VLL mass--mixing parameter space. The neutral-VLL channel gives the best sensitivity. At $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the $2σ$ exclusion reaches $\varepsilon\simeq0.013$ at $M_N=1.3~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $\varepsilon\simeq0.065$ at $M_N=2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$, while the $5σ$ discovery reach corresponds to $\varepsilon\simeq0.02$--$0.10$. At $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the charged-VLL channels probe masses up to about $2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $2.8~\mathrm{TeV}$ in the $e^\pm h$ and $e^\pm Z$ modes, respectively. These results demonstrate that a 3 TeV CLIC can provide sensitive probes of first-generation doublet VLLs over a wide mass range, including scenarios with small VLL--electron mixing.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $φ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

papers.title: Axionic Casimir Torque
papers.abstract: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.

papers.title: Probing LZ-Motivated TeV Higgsino Dark Matter through Heavier Sparticles at LHC
papers.abstract: The nearly pure TeV-scale Higgsino dark matter provides a natural explanation for the high-energy nuclear-recoil excess reported by LUX-ZEPLIN. Such a heavy and compressed Higgsino spectrum makes direct searches at the LHC challenging. We therefore investigate complementary probes through the production and decay of heavier sparticles. We perform a comprehensive analysis and obtain the following observations: (i) For a TeV Higgsino, the current LHC Run-2 searches exclude gluino up to approximately 2.2~TeV, while the HL-LHC can give an exclusion reach of 2.5--2.6~TeV and a discovery reach of 2.3--2.4~TeV; (ii) The light-flavor squark coannihilation window lies beyond the Run-2 reach, but its lower end could be excluded at the HL-LHC under optimistic assumptions; (iii) The Run-2 search does not exclude the stop or sbottom benchmarks; (iv) The slepton and heavier-electroweakino productions are too small to access at the HL-LHC.

papers.title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
papers.abstract: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

papers.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
papers.abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll φ_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > φ_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle φ\rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(φ) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

papers.title: Testing Minimal $U(2)^3$ Right-Handed Flavor Breaking in a Singlet-Scalar Vector-Like Quark Portal
papers.abstract: We study a portal of a $Z_2$-odd singlet scalar and a vector like down quark, in which a right handed flavor breaking spurion extends the portal coupling from $b_R$ to $d_R$ and $s_R$. This single coupling vector links the $b\to s$, $b\to d$, and $s\to d$ transitions. We compute the one loop dipole and $ΔF=2$ Wilson coefficients, and show that a real scalar generates no $ΔF=2$ amplitude at one loop. Using a seven observable profile likelihood of $B$ meson mixing, $ε_K$, and radiative decays, with the CKM, lattice, and short distance inputs treated as nuisance parameters, we compare a generic spurion, minimal $U(2)^3$ with a free size of the light quark couplings, and a CKM-aligned ansatz. We have found that the present data cannot yet test the flavor structure: the Standard Model is compatible with the data, with a pseudo experiment $p$-value of $0.20$, and no direction of the light quark couplings can be excluded at 95% CL. For $M_D\simeq m_{\mathcal{S}}=1$ TeV and $|λ_b|=1$, the relative light quark coupling $ε_R$ is bounded at 95% CL by $0.227$ for a generic spurion and by $0.211$ for minimal $U(2)^3$. More precise measurements of the $B_s$ mixing phase at the LHC and of $\sin2β$ at LHCb and Belle-II, together with improved lattice and CKM inputs, can make the minimality of the flavor structure testable if a deviation from the Standard Model is observed.

papers.title: Dalitz plot binning optimization for the model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ with $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays
papers.abstract: A model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ can be performed using a time-dependent analysis of $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays, where the Dalitz plots of both the $B$ and $D$ decays are divided into bins. The choice of binning scheme for the $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$ Dalitz plot directly impacts the statistical sensitivity to $β$. This paper presents an optimization of this binning using a Fisher information-based quality factor $Q^2$ and simulated annealing. The optimized binning improves the sensitivity to $β$ by approximately $10\%$ relative to the equal-phase-difference baseline, as validated by toy Monte Carlo studies without experimental effects. The robustness of this improvement against decay time acceptance, Dalitz plot efficiency, Dalitz plot resolution, and background contributions is also assessed.

papers.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice models
papers.abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/α^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

papers.title: From Dirac Neutrino Mass to Dark Radiation: An $A_4$-Symmetric FIMP Dark Matter Framework
papers.abstract: We propose a unified $A_4\times Z_2\times U(1)_L$ framework for generating small Dirac neutrino masses and address dark matter through feeble interactions in an extended particle physics model. The model extends the Standard Model with a pair of heavy vector-like neutral $A_4$ fermions $N(N_{L,R})$, two additional flavon fields $η$ and $φ$, among which $η$ being a $Z_2$-odd inert scalar and a dark-sector vector-like fermion field $χ$. We numerically explore the Dirac-sector Yukawa couplings and identify the parameter region that is consistent with the {\tt NuFit 6.1} neutrino oscillation data at the $3σ$ level. The dark matter candidate $χ$, stabilized by the $Z_2$ symmetry, is produced non-thermally through the decay $N_L\rightarrowχ+η$. By solving the Boltzmann equation, we find that the observed relic abundance, $Ω_{\rm DM}h^2\simeq0.12$, can be reproduced for freeze-in couplings of order $λ\sim10^{-5.5}$--$10^{-7.5}$ over the considered dark matter mass range. For the chosen parameter space, we also verify the interaction rate remains below the Hubble expansion rate, confirming $χ$ never reaches thermal equilibrium. Thus, our results demonstrate that the model provides a consistent realization of Dirac neutrino masses and FIMP dark matter within a common symmetry-based setup. The presence of light Dirac RH neutrinos can contribute to the dark radiation and hence the effective degrees of freedom via thermal and non-thermal processes. We further estimate the contribution of the light right-handed neutrinos to \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\), finding a maximum characteristic value of \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.14\) in the benchmark parameter region.

papers.title: Modular $S_4$ Inverse Seesaw at the LZ High-Recoil Frontier
papers.abstract: The extension of the LUX--ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil analysis to approximately $270\,\mathrm{keV}$ probes a qualitatively new dark-matter regime in which endothermic scattering can suppress conventional low-energy recoils and concentrate the surviving spectrum near the Galactic high-velocity tail. We construct a modular-$S_4$ realization in which a minimal $2N_R+2S$ inverse seesaw accounts for lepton flavor, while a separate pair of Standard-Model-singlet fermions forms the pseudo-Dirac state relevant for high-recoil xenon scattering. The sectors share a common complex modulus $τ$, so the modular forms selected by charged-lepton and neutrino data also enter the operators generating the dark Dirac mass and Majorana splitting. Our scan yields $181447$ lepton-sector solutions satisfying $χ^2_{\ell+ν}<30$, distributed among several disconnected modular regions, and predicts one effectively massless light neutrino at leading order. Restoring the physical scales allows TeV-scale heavy quasi-Dirac neutral fermions with small non-unitarity. We subsequently scan $2\times10^6$ dark-sector points only over flavor-accepted values of $τ$ and identify common-modulus solutions in the LZ-oriented region $300\,\mathrm{GeV}\le m_χ\le2\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $300\,\mathrm{keV}\leδ\le400\,\mathrm{keV}$. An exploratory two-bin Poisson likelihood, including endothermic xenon kinematics, the Helm form factor, Standard-Halo-Model velocities, Gaussian energy smearing, and profiling over the signal normalization, gives a best grid point at $(m_χ,δ)\simeq(1.847\,\mathrm{TeV},371.5\,\mathrm{keV})$, close to the terrestrial inelastic kinematic ceiling. The construction provides a direct link between modular lepton flavor, TeV-scale inverse-seesaw dynamics, and high-recoil inelastic dark matter.

papers.title: Joint Constraints on the Hubble Constant and Cosmic Baryon Density from Localized Fast Radio Bursts and DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe free-electron columns along cosmological sightlines through their dispersion measures (DMs), whereas baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) constrain cosmic expansion geometry through acoustic distance ratios. In this work, we leverage their distinct physical sensitivities to simultaneously determine the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and cosmic baryon density ($Ω_{\rm b}$) without external cosmic microwave background (CMB) or Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) priors. Combining 120 localized FRBs and DESI DR2 BAO, we obtain $H_0=71.4^{+2.2}_{-2.5}\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_{\rm b}=0.0503^{+0.0025}_{-0.0021}$ in $Λ$CDM, corresponding to precisions of $3.3\%$ and $4.6\%$, respectively. The inferred $H_0$ is statistically consistent with both SH0ES and CMB, and $Ω_{\rm b}$ agrees with the joint constraint from BBN and CMB. Adopting IllustrisTNG-based DM distributions and fixing the diffuse-gas baryon fraction tightens the constraint to $H_0=68.8\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$, but lowers the central value toward the CMB-inferred value, identifying extragalactic DM modeling as the dominant systematic uncertainty. These results establish FRB-BAO complementarity as a new avenue for simultaneously constraining $H_0$ and $Ω_{\rm b}$.

papers.title: Quantum circuit representation and incomplete Bell measurements in Compton scattering
papers.abstract: We formulate massless tree-level Compton scattering as an effective two-qubit operation on electron and photon helicities. In the Bell basis, the scattering map separates into two parity sectors and admits a simple quantum circuit representation with one nonunitary filter. After Kraus normalization, this filter defines an unsharp incomplete Bell measurement that distinguishes the two Bell-parity sectors but not the relative Bell label within each sector. We further show that the incomplete measurement alone does not surpass the classical teleportation threshold, whereas a subsequent complete Bell-basis readout enables unit conditional teleportation fidelity.

papers.title: Probing the chromo-electric dipole moment of top quark near the toponium production threshold at LHC
papers.abstract: The recent observation of an excess near the kinematic $t\bar{t}$ production threshold by the CMS and ATLAS collaborations suggests the existence of a color-singlet and $S$-wave quasi-bound state of top quark. Due to the non-relativistic nature of top and anti-top quarks in this threshold region, toponium production provides an ideal system to probe the anomalous dipole moments of the top quark. In this work, we investigate the impact of chromo-electric dipole moment (CEDM) in $t\bar{t}$-gluon vertex on toponium production at the LHC. We implement the enhanced near-threshold production of the spin-0 color-singlet toponium state $η_t$ via gluon fusion. The resonant toponium contribution is then combined with the continuum $t\bar{t}$ production amplitude, including the interference effects induced by the top CEDM. Furthermore, we construct a set of asymmetries based on the angular distributions of charged leptons in the leptonic decay channel of $t\bar{t}$. Finally, we derive the expected exclusion limit on the top quark CEDM parameter $d_t^g$ using these lepton angular asymmetries.

papers.title: A toy model for hadronic bonds in exotic hadrons
papers.abstract: Three hadronic-bond mechanisms were proposed in our previous studies to describe near-threshold exotic hadrons in terms of hadronic molecular configurations: the covalent bond arises from the sharing and exchange of valence light quarks between hadronic clusters, the creation bond originates from the activation of coherent sea $q\bar{q}$ degrees of freedom followed by the formation of effective covalent correlations, and the annihilation bond arises from valence $q\bar{q}$ annihilation and the associated mixing with a nearby compact state. A simple toy model was previously constructed only for the covalent bond, and in the present study we extend this model to incorporate the creation and annihilation bonds within a unified framework. The resulting framework organizes covalent-bond configurations as tending to lie below threshold and creation-bond configurations as tending to appear above threshold, while the annihilation bond can shift a pre-existing molecular configuration either downward or upward through mixing with a nearby compact state. An effective activation energy $E_{\rm{act}}$ is introduced for the coherent sea four-quark component involved in the creation bond, with the $Z_c(3900)$ providing the benchmark value $E_{\rm{act}}\sim17~{\rm{MeV}}$. Intriguingly, this value is numerically close to the reported mass of the $X_{17}$ particle, which we previously interpreted as a low-energy bare four-quark structure. This numerical proximity may therefore reflect common low-energy (four-quark) dynamics, although the microscopic connection remains to be established. For the isoscalar $D^*\bar{D}^*B^*\bar{B}^*$ configuration involving the $Z_c(4020)$ and $Z_b(10650)$ creation-bond subsystems linked by two additional covalent bonds, we estimate a binding energy of approximately $36~{\rm{MeV}}$ below its four-meson threshold and propose searches in the $4μ$ and $4\mu2π$ final states.

papers.title: Primordial Graviton Entanglement in Quasicrystalline Inflation
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement structure of gravitons in quasicrystalline inflation. Both parity-even and parity-odd interactions generate graviton pairs with nonzero total momentum. For opposite-helicity pairs with identical momenta, the parity-even contribution can be nonzero, whereas the parity-odd contribution vanishes. The transition from inflation to radiation domination produces additional conventional two-mode squeezing. We derive the resulting normal and anomalous covariances. The initially nonzero reciprocal blocks of the full field-momentum covariance remain nonzero under homogeneous evolution, although individual components can vanish. We show that this homogeneous, helicity-preserving evolution acts unitarily within each helicity sector and therefore preserves the entanglement between the complete right- and left-helicity sectors. Nevertheless, it can eliminate entanglement in the reduced state of a co-propagating pair. We illustrate this distinction using a solvable four-mode model.

papers.title: When hadrons collide: di-J/psi structure in the final state
papers.abstract: The structures in the di-J/psi spectrum seen at the LHC are widely read as fully charmed tetraquarks. As an alternative scenario, the $2^{++}$ production amplitude for a compact $cc\bar c\bar c$ source rescattering through ten charmonium-pair channels is presented. The model is completely fixed except for three background parameters and provides a competitive description of the data, with chi-sq/ndf=56/50. Prominent features are driven by J/psi psi(nS) thresholds or threshold enhancement, with no need for exotic hadrons.

papers.title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
papers.abstract: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.

papers.title: Theoretical calculations for $t{\bar t}H$ production
papers.abstract: We calculate higher-order perturbative corrections for $t{\bar t}H$ production. By adding second-order and third-order soft-gluon corrections to NLO QCD and NLO electroweak (EW) results, we present total and differential cross sections at LHC energies through approximate N$^3$LO (aN$^3$LO) in QCD and NLO in EW. Our aN$^3$LO QCD + NLO EW results provide significant enhancements and a reduced scale dependence for the cross section and the top-quark transverse-momentum and rapidity distributions.

papers.title: BSMScanner: a lightweight framework for beyond-the-Standard-Model global fits
papers.abstract: We present BSMScanner, a framework in which a beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) parameter scan is specified as a set of declarative YAML documents rather than written as a program. The user declares the free parameters and their priors, the mass matrices and the diagonalisations that act on them, the observables, the theory-validity conditions and the likelihood terms. The framework validates this specification, resolves it into a dependency graph and compiles it once into a typed C++ evaluation kernel, which is then driven by an independently chosen scanning engine: uniform sampling, two differential-evolution engines, or a staged basin-discovery orchestrator, optionally followed by Markov-chain posterior refinement. Flavour physics matrix diagonalisation, PMNS and CKM construction in fixed conventions, tabulated oscillation likelihoods and a library of common flavour observables are provided by the framework and imported by name, so that a model file contains only model-specific definitions; quantities without a closed form, such as a relic density, enter through a C++ or Python plugin interface. We describe the specification schema, the observable and likelihood library, the scanning engines and their configuration, and demonstrate the framework on six benchmark models with $4$ to $26$ free parameters, giving for each the specification, the scan configuration, the resulting best fit and analytic cross-checks of the result.

papers.title: Chiral mass corrections to decuplet hidden-charm pentaquark states
papers.abstract: We calculate the masses of the $J^P=\frac{1}{2}^-$ hidden-charm pentaquark states in the $SU(3)$ decuplet within the heavy pentaquark chiral perturbation theory (HPChPT) up to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The one-loop self-energy corrections from the $π$, $K$, and $η$ mesons are evaluated. Taking $P_ψ^N(4312)$ and $P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)$ as inputs, we predict the masses of the doubly-strange and triply-strange decuplet members $P_{ψss}^N$ and $P_{ψsss}^Λ$ to be 4.607 GeV and 4.755 GeV, respectively. The mass splittings between adjacent strangeness layers are nearly constant at approximately 0.148 GeV. This equal-spacing pattern follows directly from the analytical structure of the NLO chiral corrections, while its actual magnitude is set by the low-energy constants (LECs). It indicates that the Gell--Mann--Okubo (GMO) relation, expected at the leading order of SU(3) flavor symmetry breaking, persists to good accuracy at the NLO.

papers.title: Probing eV-scale sterile neutrinos with neutrinoless double-beta decay and beta decay
papers.abstract: An eV-scale sterile Majorana neutrino can suppress neutrinoless double-beta decay through destructive interference with the active-neutrino contribution, weakening the resulting constraints on sterile-neutrino parameters. We investigate how complementary beta-decay information restricts this cancellation in the 3+1 framework. Using updated oscillation parameters that include the first JUNO results, we determine the allowed sterile-neutrino mass and mixing regions for both normal and inverted ordering. We show that an upper limit on the effective beta-decay mass $m_β$ of the three light neutrinos strengthens the constraints from neutrinoless double-beta decay alone. The beta-decay bound restricts the light-neutrino masses and hence the cancellation between the active and sterile contributions to $m_{ββ}$. We derive analytic expressions for the resulting boundaries and use complex-plane geometry to explain the allowed values of the sterile Majorana phase $α_4$ for a finite $|m_{ββ}|$ limit. For the mixing considered, normal ordering allows a broad range of $α_4$ at small sterile masses, whereas inverted ordering favors values near $π$. The allowed phase range narrows as the sterile mass approaches its upper bound or the limit on $|m_{ββ}|$ becomes more stringent.

papers.title: On some nonlinear extensions to Maxwell's electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Soon after Maxwell's celebrated synthesis of electrodynamics, the discovery of the electron raised fundamental questions about the nature and structure of elementary particles. The picture of a small, rigid, charged body of finite radius faced the difficulty of introducing non-electromagnetic forces or stresses to prevent the charge from dispersing, an assumption that was increasingly regarded as unsatisfactory. The alternative description in terms of a point charge was no more satisfactory, because its electromagnetic self-energy diverges. From the early twentieth century onward, several authors therefore explored modifications of Maxwell's theory, with nonlinear electrodynamics emerging as a particularly natural and radical possibility. In this paper, we revisit at the undergraduate level some of the nonlinear theories proposed in this context and explore their ability to address the classical self-energy problem of charged particles.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength. The lifetime of the sound wave source increases with decreasing $α$: for weaker transitions the source can persist for longer than a Hubble time, while for stronger transitions it decays within a Hubble time. When the walls propagate as deflagrations, the GW spectral shape changes drastically, with steeper ultraviolet tails and a shorter-lived sound wave source. We also observe that the magnitude of the normalized GWs is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than obtained in the Minkowski spacetime simulations.

papers.title: $χ_{c0}$ production in $\barΛn$ scattering process
papers.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the production of $χ_{c0}$ in the $\barΛ n \rightarrow χ_{c0} K^{0}_{S}$ process by utilizing an effective Lagrangian approach. Based on the $χ_{c0} \rightarrow n K^{0}_{S} \barΛ$ decay observed by the BESIII Collaboration, the coupling constants are determined by fitting the $M_{K^{0}_{S} \barΛ}$ and $M_{n K^{0}_{S}}$ invariant mass spectra, where eight $N$ and $Λ$ state are considered. Moreover, the parameters $β$ is taken to be 1, 2, 3 as special cases to check the parameter dependence. Our results show that two clear structures can be observed in both $M_{K^{0}_{S} \barΛ}$ and $M_{n K^{0}_{S}}$ invariant mass spectra, which should correspond to $N(1720)/N(1895)$ and $Λ(1600)/Λ(1890)$, respectively. In addition, the contributions from $N(938)$ and $Λ(1116)$ intermediate states are much smaller than those of the above-threshold resonances. With the fitted parameters for $β=1$, 2, 3, the cross sections for $\barΛ n \rightarrow χ_{c0} K^{0}_{S}$ are estimated to be 1.9 nb, 4.2 nb, and 8.0 nb at $\sqrt{s}=6$ GeV, respectively. Furthermore, our estimations indicate that the differential cross sections for $\barΛ n \rightarrow χ_{c0} K^{0}_{S}$ reach a maximum in the forward angle region.

papers.title: Mixed leptogenesis sources and low-energy neutrino portals
papers.abstract: A mixed leptogenesis source and its low-energy neutrino portal depend on the same heavy-particle amplitudes. We determine how this common origin restricts matching cancellations and the scalar population produced during reheating. For two Majorana mass levels, each containing a degenerate pair, the inclusive lepton-number-violating invariant fixes an allowed norm domain for the mixed dimension-five coefficient at specified threshold strengths. An aligned flavour texture makes the conventional source vanish as a matrix and gives equal coupling norms for the two massive neutrinos. A continuous family preserves the neutrino-mass fit while relating the source to unequal light coupling strengths. The matched couplings give benchmark vacuum lifetimes of $1.62\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $2.80\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{s}$, while reheating normalized to the baryon abundance determines the primary spectrum. In the massless Born approximation with dilute outgoing states, bath-produced scalars carry $4.81\times10^{-5}$ of the primary scalar energy but contribute $11.1$ times its variance. The positive production functional converts the matching constraint into a conditional variance bound. We derive the scalar-mass dependence of stimulated emission and the Hartree moment equation, keeping the scalar mass and quartic as renormalized matching inputs. These results link the leptogenesis source to light-neutrino decay and the finite-density quantities entering subsequent coupled transport.

papers.title: Seeking a possible approach to understanding the origin of the proton mass using twist-4 contributions in inclusive reactions
papers.abstract: Most of the mass of the visible universe originates from the strong interaction. Quantitatively reproducing the origin of the nucleon mass is one of the important challenges in fundamental science. Since the next-generation Electron-Ion Collider has identified resolving this problem as one of its major goals, further theoretical studies are needed to develop approaches to investigating the origin experimentally. In this paper, we explore the possibility of evaluating the ``gluon condensate term'' which is particularly difficult to determine among the contributions to the nucleon mass, using high-energy scattering experiments. We first express the gluon condensate term in terms of experimentally accessible twist-4 lightcone matrix elements. We then derive, for the first time, analytic formulas for the cross section including all twist-4 contributions from pure quark, quark-gluon, and pure gluon matrix elements in $ep$ collisions, and show how these contributions can be related to the gluon condensate term.

papers.title: Factorisation theorem and pole cancellation in the resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at NLO
papers.abstract: We study the subleading resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ contribution to the inclusive decay $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at next-to-leading order (NLO) in $α_s$. We present a formulation of the factorisation theorem which is valid beyond the leading order (LO). On this basis, we explicitly demonstrate the cancellation of all $1/\varepsilon$ singularities between the hard, hard-collinear, anti-hard-collinear and soft contributions. For this purpose, a central result of this work is the computation of the $u$-integrated massless two-loop anti-hard-collinear jet function, which determines the structure of the $1/\varepsilon$ singularities. In addition, we compute the hard function at the required order, combine our results with the hard-collinear jet function known from the literature, and employ the shape function whose renormalisation was determined in our previous work. There, we showed, for inclusive as well as for exclusive modes, that certain contributions to these multi-light-cone soft functions are physically irrelevant and can be consistently omitted; the explicit cancellation of the corresponding divergences provides a non-trivial confirmation of this statement. Overall, our findings constitute a non-trivial consistency check of the factorisation framework for this subleading resolved contribution at NLO and provide the basis for a full phenomenological analysis.

papers.title: Disappearing Tracks from Electroweak Vector Dark Matter at the LHC
papers.abstract: We study the disappearing-track signature of a spin-1 minimal dark matter candidate transforming in the real five-dimensional representation of $SU(2)_L$ with vanishing hypercharge. Radiative electroweak corrections induce a compressed mass spectrum among the multiplet components, allowing the singly charged state $V^\pm$ to attain a macroscopic lifetime and decay via $V^\pm \to V^0 π^\pm$ inside tracking detectors. We recast the ATLAS search for disappearing tracks with the full Run-2 dataset of $137\text{ fb}^{-1}$, originally targeted at long-lived charginos, computing the tracklet reconstruction probability analytically from the published efficiency so that the full lifetime range is covered. The procedure reproduces the ATLAS limits for pure winos within $6\%$ in mass. The Run-2 data exclude quintuplet masses up to $1080\text{ GeV}$ for proper decay lengths $cτ\simeq 250\text{ mm}$, and $M_V < 630\text{ GeV}$ for a mass splitting of $166\text{ MeV}$. For the radiative mass splitting predicted by the model with a small Higgs-portal coupling, masses between $120\text{ GeV}$ and $240\text{--}300\text{ GeV}$ are excluded. With $3\text{ ab}^{-1}$ and a Run-2-like analysis, the sensitivity would extend to $1750\text{ GeV}$ for vanishing background and to $1530\text{ GeV}$ for a linear extrapolation of the instrumental background.

papers.title: Collider and direct detection as key probes of asymmetric dark matter: Signals from a compressed Inert Higgs doublet
papers.abstract: The cosmic imbalance of particles over antiparticles may be inherited by the dark matter in a certain class of asymmetric dark matter models. In this article, we thoroughly investigate the signatures of the minimal realization of this idea. In this model a new (stable) inert Higgs, $H'$, plays the role of the mediator that facilitates the asymmetry transfer from the visible to the dark sector. It also constitutes a small dark matter sub-component, while the dominant component stems from a singlet scalar asymmetry. A combination of phenomenological and cosmological constraints requires this new inert Higgs doublet to be quite light $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}< 580\,{\rm GeV}$ and its spectrum rather compressed, $ΔM = m_{H^\pm}-m_{H_0} \lesssim 1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $δm = m_{A_0}-m_{H_0}\lesssim 5\,{\rm MeV}$. Therefore its charged component can be relatively long-lived on collider length-scales. By recasting searches for compressed Higgsinos at the LHC, we derive new limits on this particle and show that, while at present most of the parameter space for this state is still unconstrained, large and key regions of parameter space will be tested at the HL-LHC by a combination of searches for disappearing charged tracks and displaced soft tracks. Quite remarkably, the lifetime of the charged component of the doublet can be correlated with the dark matter interaction rate at direct detection experiments and we show that the next generation of direct detection experiments has a unique sensitivity to the parameter space in the model. The fact that a small neutral mass splitting is a prediction of the asymmetric setup makes it an interesting candidate to account for the high energy nuclear recoil event recently reported by the LZ experiment. More generally, our detailed phenomenological study holds for any dark matter model involving an inert Higgs doublet with mass below 580 GeV.

papers.title: Solutions of Roy equations for variable pion mass
papers.abstract: The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pion masses below the physical value in the region between threshold and $s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that the phenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentially unchanged. Moreover, for $M_π\le M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiral perturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengths provide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. The outcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves as the light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test of the approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$, $P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreement with chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_π\le M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion masses above the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resulting solutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_π=239\MeV$. The present work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fully incorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependence of the $σ$ and $ρ$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both of which will be addressed in future work.

papers.title: A Witten effect for global monopoles
papers.abstract: Global monopoles can carry electric charge even when the scalar field that forms them is neutral. We show that a CP-odd operator in the Goldstone effective theory, typically discarded as a total derivative, gives them an electric charge $Q=-Cn$, with $C$ its Wilson coefficient and $n$ the winding number. This is a Witten effect on a global defect, generated by a mixed $θ$-term between electromagnetism and a composite connection built from the Goldstone fields. The same group theory condition that allows the operator also guarantees the existence of monopoles. We also give a fermionic UV completion and determine the coefficient by matching the Goldstone-Wilczek current.

papers.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
papers.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

papers.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
papers.abstract: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. The cost of tokenization is evaluated on tasks including jet $p_T$ regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. We find that tokenization preserves much of the information needed for these tasks at compression factors of approximately 4-11$\times$ while keeping the jet $p_T$ resolution below 1%. We also present heptokens, an open-source library for tokenizing HEP data.

papers.title: Complete four-loop pressure of cold QED
papers.abstract: Extending the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of a cold and dense ultrarelativistic electron gas to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in the gauge coupling has remained an open problem since the classic N2LO result of Freedman and McLerran, published in 1977. Here, we present the full N3LO pressure, the first thermodynamic quantity determined to this order in a physical gauge theory. The pressure exhibits good perturbative convergence and weak renormalization-scale dependence even at sizable couplings, while a Bayesian analysis of missing higher-order contributions indicates uncertainties that can exceed those inferred from scale variation alone.

papers.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
papers.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

papers.title: Long-Distance Contributions to Light Vector Mesons and Radiative Decays of $η_{c}$
papers.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the long-distance contributions to light hadrons and radiative decays of $η_c$, where the long-distance contribution is phenomenologically described by the meson loops. Our estimations indicate that the branching fractions of $η_c \to \mathcal{VV},\ \mathcal{V}=(ρ,ω, φ)$ can be roughly reproduced in the range $1.4<α<1.6$. While the parameter range for $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}$ is determined by the similarity of $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$ and $χ_{c1} \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$. In this parameter range, our estimations indicate that the branching fractions for the processes $η_c \to γρ^0$ and $η_c \to γω$ are of order $10^{-4}$, while the one for the process $η_c \to γφ$ is of order $10^{-5}$. The estimations in the present work are expected to be accessible by future experiments at BESIII and Belle II.

papers.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
papers.abstract: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

papers.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
papers.abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

papers.title: ALP interactions with mesons and baryons at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$: a general field redefinition invariant approach
papers.abstract: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. Using LSZ reduction, we choose fields for which ALP--meson mixing vanishes at this order; amplitudes then depend only on direct invariant couplings, while the anomalous gluonic interaction remains encoded in the $U(1)_A$ sector. For the baryon octet, we derive the general vector and axial couplings and identify, to our knowledge for the first time, an independent invariant ALP--baryon interaction from a second topological singlet structure in the $U(3)$ baryon Lagrangian. We constrain flavour-changing couplings with rare hyperon decays and show in an explicit ultraviolet model that running and matching can generate them from flavour-diagonal high-scale couplings. Finally, we estimate baryon--antibaryon widths and find that, in a gluophilic benchmark, their sum can exceed individual exclusive mesonic widths for $2~\text{GeV} \le m_a \le 3~\text{GeV}$.

papers.title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
papers.abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.

papers.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

papers.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.
